items.title: Paris Folding Sequence Production
items.text: The visual effects team enhanced a sequence captured with six high-speed cameras by adding destruction and debris, while green screen and CGI handled the Paris folding scene.
items.reason: The proposal text accurately reflects the evidence quote regarding camera usage, VFX enhancement, and green screen/CGI for the Paris folding sequence without adding external claims.
items.evidence_quote: Pfister used six high-speed cameras to capture the sequence from different angles and make sure that they got the shot. The visual effects department enhanced the sequence, adding more destruction and flying debris. For the "Paris folding" sequence and when Ariadne "creates" the bridges, green screen and CGI were used on location.[11]: 17

items.evidence_quote: In addition Nolan and Pfister tested using Showscan and Super Dimension 70 as potential large-format, high-frame-rate camera systems to use for the film, but ultimately decided against either format.[33]: 29

items.title: What is the specific objective of the job offered to Dom Cobb by Saito?
options: To extract information from Robert Fischer's subconscious regarding his father's conglomerate.
To implant the idea in Robert Fischer that he should dissolve his father's conglomerate.
To layer multiple dreams within each other to infiltrate a target's subconscious.
To clear Cobb's criminal status by performing espionage on Maurice Fischer.
items.reason: Option 3 describes a technique (layering dreams) rather than the specific objective of the job; Option 2 is the only correct answer, making the other options invalid distractors.
items.evidence_quote: Dom Cobb and Arthur are professional thieves who perform corporate espionage using experimental dream-sharing technology to infiltrate their targets' subconscious and extract information. Their latest target Saito is impressed with Cobb's ability to layer multiple dreams within each other. He offers to hire Cobb for the ostensibly impossible job of performing "inception": implanting Robert Fischer, the son of Saito's competitor Maurice Fischer, with the idea to dissolve his father's conglomerate.

items.title: What does Saito promise in return for Cobb completing the inception job?
options: A large sum of money and a new contract for future corporate espionage.
Public recognition as the greatest dream architect in the world.
To clear Cobb's criminal status, allowing him to return home to his children.
Immunity from prosecution for all past crimes committed before the job.
items.reason: Option 3 is the correct answer based on the evidence quote. Options 1 and 4 are incorrect because Saito does not promise money, new contracts, or general immunity for past crimes.
items.evidence_quote: In return, Saito promises to clear Cobb's criminal status, allowing him to return home to his children.
